[Fix eu-11-x, 2026-10-25] Munster is drawn without kingdom-of-desmond's 1177 region until 1595 (the Desmond page: 'After the death of King Donal IX MacCarthy Mor in 1596', infobox 'Disestablished: 1596'); the modern province overlapped 26 H3 cells of it. Cliopatria's Irish Catholic Confederation shapes (1642-1652, 44-61 thousand km2) and Commonwealth shapes overlap.

Cliopatria's Kingdom of England (to 1708) and Kingdom of Great Britain (from 1709) shapes already contain the island, so this keyframe duplicates theirs; the renderer should draw it only as the dependency tint.

region.text: the Pale, where Dublin governed in 1542 (without the Kavanagh lands in Wicklow)

ledger.note: 1542: Henry VIII becomes King of Ireland. 'Crown of Ireland Act, 18 June 1542' and 'This act declared King Henry VIII of England as the King of Ireland.' The Lordship became a kingdom in personal union with England; Dublin ruled only the Pale.

region.text: Thomond (Clare, Limerick and North Tipperary), surrendered and regranted: Murchadh made Earl of Thomond

ledger.note: 1543: Thomond submits. The Thomond page: Murchadh 'agreed to surrender and regrant to the Tudor state' and 'was made Earl of Thomond', tied to a Limerick parliament of 1542; its infobox gives 1543 as the end of Thomond. 1543 mirrors kingdom-of-thomond's dissolve; the page's own year for the surrender is 1542.

region.text: King's County and Queen's County (Laois and Offaly), the Plantation of 1556

ledger.counterpart: Gaelic Irish lordships of Laois and Offaly
ledger.note: 1556: the first plantation. 'The first such scheme was the Plantation of King's County', named for Philip and Mary, with Philipstown and Maryborough renamed. The page names the plantation, not its owners; Laois-Offaly is the researcher's reading of 'King's County'.

region.text: Munster without the Desmond kingdom's western half (held by the MacCarthy Mor to 1595) and without Thomond (gained in 1543), whose Desmond estates were confiscated after the Second Desmond Rebellion (without the Kavanagh lands)

ledger.note: 1583: the Desmond Rebellions end and Munster passes to the Crown. 'their estates were confiscated by the Crown' after the Second Desmond Rebellion (1579-83); 'In 1584, the Surveyor General of Ireland ... surveyed Munster'. The Tudor conquest article dates the rebellions '(1569-1573, 1579-1583)'. The year is the end of the rebellion; the page gives no date for the confiscation. [Fix eu-11-x, 2026-10-25] The region excludes kingdom-of-desmond's land (the gain follows in 1596) and Thomond (1543).

region.text: Monaghan, surrendered and regranted: 'with his territory becoming County Monaghan in the Tudor Kingdom of Ireland'

ledger.note: 1585: Airgialla ends. 'The Kingdom of Airgialla came to an end in 1585 when' Rossa Boy MacMahon 'agreed to surrender and regrant his territories to the English Crown in Ireland'.

region.text: Connacht, whose chiefs' countries became baronies of the counties under the Composition

ledger.counterpart: Gaelic lordships of Connacht (the Composition of Connacht)
ledger.note: 1585: the Composition of Connacht. 'The Composition of Connacht, or Composition of Connaught and Thomond, was a 1585 agreement'; 'Connacht was made a Presidency in 1569 and divided into counties afterwards, but the county administration did not function efficiently until the Composition'. The Crown's effective hold begins here; the page lists no particular lordship (confidence 2). Closes the first version's gap for Connacht 1556-1602 (nobody drew it between the end of kingdom-of-connacht in 1474 and 1603).

region.text: Ulster, 'the only province that was completely outside English control'

ledger.note: 1593: the Nine Years' War begins in Ulster. 'the Nine Years' War (1593-1603)'; it 'reached Munster in 1598' and the Munster settlers were chased off their lands (Plantations page). Ulster as the zone is the researcher's reading of the Plantations page. [Reviewer eu-11-x, 2026-10-25] Counterpart was the string "Hugh O'Neill, Earl of Tyrone (the Ulster confederacy)"; set to tir-eoghain, whose dossier carries the mirror contest pair 1593-1603 (Tír Eoghain page: Aodh Mór Ó Néill, Earl of Tyrone, 'fled in 1607').

region.text: the western Desmond lands (Cork and Kerry without the 60 km round Cork): 'After the death of King Donal IX MacCarthy Mor in 1596'

ledger.note: 1596: the Kingdom of Desmond ends. Desmond page: 'After the death of King Donal IX MacCarthy Mor in 1596' and infobox 'Disestablished: 1596'; 'the former Kingdom of Desmond was partitioned between County Cork and County Kerry (in 1606)'. The page does not say the Crown took the land in 1596; 2 because the year is the page's and the taker the researcher's reading (mirrors kingdom-of-desmond's dissolve).

region.text: the rest of the island: Ulster without Monaghan and Tyrone, Connacht and the remaining Gaelic lordships; 'by 1603 the entire country was under English rule'

ledger.counterpart: Gaelic Irish lordships (Tyrone's confederacy and the rest)
ledger.note: 1603: the whole island under the Crown. 'by 1603 the entire country was under English rule.' The Flight of the Earls (1607) and the plantation of Ulster 'in the 1610s' (Plantations page) followed. [Fix eu-11-x, 2026-10-25] Region now leaves out Monaghan (1585), Tyrone (1607) and the Leinster remnant (separate 1603 gain from kingdom-of-leinster). Connacht (1585) also left out.

region.text: the last Leinster lands (Wexford, Carlow, Wicklow) of the MacMurrough-Kavanagh kingdom: 'it became part of the Tudor Kingdom of Ireland'

ledger.note: 1603: the Kavanagh kingdom of Leinster ends. Mirrors kingdom-of-leinster's 1603 dissolve (confidence 2 there); the Kingdom of Ireland page's 'forced Tyrone to submit in 1603, completing the Tudor conquest of Ireland' dates the end of Gaelic resistance.

region.text: Ulster; Tyrone submitted

ledger.note: 1603: Tyrone submits. 'forced Tyrone to submit in 1603, completing the Tudor conquest of Ireland'; the Kingdom of Ireland infobox gives 'Treaty of Mellifont, 30 March 1603'. [Reviewer eu-11-x, 2026-10-25] Counterpart was the string "Hugh O'Neill, Earl of Tyrone (the Ulster confederacy)"; set to tir-eoghain, whose dossier carries the mirror contest pair 1593-1603 (Tír Eoghain page: Aodh Mór Ó Néill, Earl of Tyrone, 'fled in 1607').

region.text: Tyrone, Derry, Limavady and Inishowen, forfeit after the Flight of the Earls

ledger.note: 1607: Tir Eoghain ends. Tir Eoghain page: Aodh Mor O Neill, Earl of Tyrone, 'fled in 1607 in what became known as the Flight of the Earls'; infobox 'Disestablished: 1607'. The Plantations page (read for tir-eoghain) has the earls leaving in 1607 and the lands forfeit. Mirrors tir-eoghain's 1607 dissolve.

region.text: 'most of Ireland except for east and west Ulster, Cork city and Dublin'

ledger.note: 1642: the Confederation of Kilkenny takes most of the island. 'From 1642 to 1649, the Confederates controlled most of Ireland except for east and west Ulster, Cork city and Dublin.' The page dates the Confederation both May and October 1642; the war began with the Rebellion of 1641 in Ulster. The 'Cessation of Arms' with the Royalists was signed on 15 September 1643.

region.text: 'Ireland was occupied and annexed by the English Commonwealth, a republic which lasted until 1660'

ledger.note: 1653: Ireland is annexed by the Commonwealth. The last organised Irish force 'surrendered in Cavan in April 1653' and the infobox says Ireland was 'annexed by the Commonwealth of England'; the Kingdom of Ireland infobox lists 'Commonwealth, 1652-1660'. The page does not say the kingdom continued as a separate entity after 1653.

region.text: Ireland returns to the Crown with the Restoration: the island, taken back from the Commonwealth

ledger.note: 1660: the Commonwealth ends and Ireland returns to a Stuart king. The Kingdom of Ireland page: infobox 'Commonwealth: 1652-1660', 'During the subsequent interregnum period, England, Scotland and Ireland were ruled as a republic until 1660' and 'The kingdom's order was restored 1660 with the restoration of Charles II'; that page gives the year only. The month is May, from the Commonwealth of England page: 'On 8 May it proclaimed that King Charles II had been the lawful monarch since the execution of Charles I in January 1649' (Charles returned on 23 May and entered London on 29 May); the commonwealth-of-england dossier ends the state in May 1660. Fx-52 (K07): the type was 'split', which gives the splitting state's own cells to the counterpart; Ireland held nothing after the 1653 merge, so the compiler moved the island's cells to the Commonwealth instead of to Ireland (the root of the Irish hole of 1662-1699, patched in p1660-p1669 events/3-5). It is a 'gain': Ireland takes the island from the Commonwealth, the mirror of the 1653 merge above. The commonwealth-of-england dossier now also names kingdom-of-ireland first-hand in its identity.successors.

region.text: Ireland, where James II landed with French troops; 'In March 1689' Hamilton secured eastern Ulster

ledger.note: 1689: James II lands at Kinsale. 'James landed in Kinsale on 12 March' 1689; the Jacobites held most of the island, the Williamite holdouts were Derry (besieged April to 28 July 1689) and Enniskillen.

region.text: Ireland; the Jacobite army surrendered at Limerick

ledger.note: 1691: the Treaty of Limerick ends the war. 'Sarsfield signed the Treaty of Limerick with Ginkel on 3 October 1691'; Aughrim was fought on 12 July 1691.

region.text: the whole island, a separate kingdom 'subordinate' to the crown of Great Britain

ledger.note: 1707: Ireland becomes a dependency of Great Britain. Kingdom of Ireland page: it 'was a dependency of England from 1542 to 1707, and then of Great Britain from 1707 to 1800'; its subordinate status was 'enshrined in the Declaratory Act 1719'. Mirrors kingdom-of-great-britain's vassal_start of 1707/5; 1707 is the year of the Acts of Union that created Great Britain; the colony type already supplies the tint, so the pair only mirrors the Great Britain dossier.

region.text: the whole island

ledger.note: 1800: the dependency ends with the Act of Union (31 December 1800); the kingdom merges with Great Britain on 1 January 1801 into the United Kingdom (see the dissolve below). Mirrors kingdom-of-great-britain's vassal_end of 1800/12.

region.text: the whole island

ledger.note: 1800: the Act of Union. 'Act of Union, 31 December 1800' (infobox); 'the Kingdom of Ireland merged on 1 January 1801 with the Kingdom of Great Britain.' The Irish Parliament ceased to exist; the executive under the Lord Lieutenant remained to 1922. [Reviewer eu-11-x, 2026-10-25] Counterpart was kingdom-of-great-britain, whose dossier itself dissolves on 31 December 1800 into united-kingdom; the merged state of 1 January 1801 is the United Kingdom.

wars.name: Desmond Rebellions
wars.outcome: Crown victory; the Desmond estates were confiscated and Munster was planted with English settlers.
wars.note: Dated '(1569-1573, 1579-1583)' on the Tudor conquest page.

wars.name: Nine Years' War (Ireland)
wars.outcome: Crown victory: Tyrone submitted in 1603 and the Crown held the whole island; the Flight of the Earls followed in 1607.

wars.name: Irish Confederate Wars
wars.outcome: 23 October 1641 to 27 April 1653: the Confederates held most of the island 1642-1649; the Cromwellian conquest annexed Ireland to the Commonwealth.

wars.name: Williamite war in Ireland
wars.outcome: Williamite victory: Derry relieved 28 July 1689, the Boyne 1 July 1690, Aughrim 12 July 1691, Treaty of Limerick 3 October 1691.

certainty.note: The Crown's real authority is the Pale, then bits of Leinster and Munster; the pages draw no line.
The island's coast is the frontier; internal control is complete only as a claim.
Confederate, Covenanter, Royalist and Parliamentarian zones shifted yearly.

notes: Typed colony because it was a dependency of the Crown of England (then Great Britain); the Lordship (1171-1542) is a separate dossier and the 1542 act is the dividing line the pages use. Cliopatria has no Kingdom of Ireland; its Kingdom of England (1210-1708) and Kingdom of Great Britain (1709+) shapes already include Irish land, so the England and Great Britain dossiers (other parts) should either subtract these keyframes or the renderer treat this as a tint over them. The surrender and regrant policy, the Ulster plantation of the 1610s and the Penal Laws were not opened; Connacht 1556-1602 is a gap. The 1782 Constitution ('Poynings' Law was repealed in 1782') moved no border. Not covered: the Kildare Rebellion is in the Lordship dossier. [Fix eu-11-x, 2026-10-25] After the review: (1) Munster is drawn without kingdom-of-desmond's western half until 1595 (26 cells were double-filled 1584-1596) and the 1596 gain from kingdom-of-desmond is added; (2) 1543 gain of Thomond from kingdom-of-thomond (Clare, Limerick, North Tipperary were drawn by nobody 1543-1583); (3) 1585 gain of Monaghan from airgialla; (4) the 1603 whole-island keyframe now excludes tir-eoghain's shape until 1607 and a 1607 gain cp tir-eoghain is added (the alternative, a vassal pair 1603-1607, was not used because neither the Tir Eoghain nor the Kingdom of Ireland page calls Tyrone a vassal); the Leinster remnant (Wexford, Carlow, Wicklow) is a separate 1603 gain cp kingdom-of-leinster; (5) the five dossiers that name this state as successor are now predecessors; (6) the vassal pair 1707/5-1800/12 cp kingdom-of-great-britain mirrors that dossier. Boundary years: kingdom-of-thomond's last keyframe runs to 1543 and kingdom-of-leinster's to 1603, so the two shapes are double-filled in those single dissolve years; the Pale keyframes touch the Kavanagh lands (kingdom-of-leinster, 1375-1603) in about 6 cells. Connacht is now drawn from 1585 (Composition of Connacht page, confidence 2). Still open: the 1653-1659 merge, which commonwealth-of-england does not mirror. [Fix eu-11-x, 2026-10-25] The pre-1603 shapes now exclude the Leinster remnant (Wexford, Carlow, Wicklow), which kingdom-of-leinster draws to 1603 and which this state gains in 1603.
